annotations.title: Create a Help Center (no account needed)

description:
Create a new HelpCenter.io help center for the user, with no account and no sign-in: the first step of building or migrating a help center for someone who does not have HelpCenter.io yet.

What it returns (also as structuredContent): site_id, subdomain, api_key, claim_url, expires_at, limits, docs_url.
  - api_key: this help center's agent key, shown ONLY in this result. Every other tool here that acts on the help center REQUIRES it as agent_key: pass it on each call, exactly as returned, for the rest of the task. This connection has no sign-in, so the key cannot become its credential; the argument is how each call proves which help center it acts on. Keep it to yourself: never show it to the user, write it into content, or send it anywhere but agent_key.
  - site_id: the help center's id, for helpcenter_get_help_center and helpcenter_discard_help_center.
  - claim_url: the link the user claims the help center with (they sign up or sign in and verify their email). Give it to the user once the help center is ready. Nothing is emailed to them.

The help center starts private and hidden from search engines, on a temporary address, and is deleted 7 days after creation (expires_at) unless the user claims it. Until it is claimed it holds at most 500 articles (drafts included), 100 categories and 5 languages, and answers only its content and design tools.

Next: fill it — helpcenter_scan_import for a public Zendesk, Intercom, Document360, Help Scout, Front or HelpDocs help center, or helpcenter_create_category and helpcenter_create_article / helpcenter_bulk_create_articles, giving each article the external_id of its address at the source; check it with helpcenter_get_help_center, whose preview_url shows the help center as its readers will see it; then give the user claim_url.

Limits: in ChatGPT, whose connection carries OpenAI's client certificate, creation counts in OpenAI's shared pool, an hourly and an open-at-once allowance across every ChatGPT agent. From any other client it counts in this connector's own pool: 60 help centers an hour and 300 open at once, across every agent using the connector. Migration requests are limited to 30 a day across every agent using the connector, ChatGPT included. On limit_reached or capacity_reached, file a migration request with helpcenter_request_migration instead: it creates the help centers too, up to 50 at once.

Each call creates another help center: call it once per help center the user wants.

Args:
  - name (string, required): usually the user's product or company. 1-100 characters.
  - source_url (string, optional): the knowledge base you are migrating, if any.
  - language (string, optional): the default language, e.g. 'en' (the default), 'de'.

language.description: The help center's default language, as a locale code: 'en' (the default), 'de', 'pt-BR', 'zh-Hans'...

name.description: The help center's name, usually the user's product or company. A name containing a protected brand name is refused (name_blocked).

source_url.description: The https address of the knowledge base you are migrating, if any. Kept for HelpCenter.io's migration team and used as the default source of a migration request; never fetched by this call.

name: helpcenter_create_help_center
title: Create a Help Center (no account needed)
